explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly compares LLM-as-Judge (SwiLTra-Judge setups) with human expert scores on the same 400 annotated samples, reports Spearman correlations, conducts statistical significance tests, and evaluates alignment between LLM and human judgments.

prompts.notes: Exact prompts shown in Appendix listings 5 (detailed) and 6 (codebook). Tested two absolute grading styles (basic and detailed) and one deduction grading style (codebook).

inter_annotator_agreement.interpretation: Moderate agreement for laws (0.56), fair agreement for headnotes (0.41)

guidelines.notes: Annotation guidelines with point deduction system provided in Appendix G. Experts used 0-100 scale focusing on completeness and accuracy with predefined deductions for legal terminology errors.

sample_size.notes: Originally 400 samples annotated by human experts, but 32 samples (8%) where experts disagreed by ≥30 points were excluded for higher confidence validation

quantitative_scores.notes: Average correlation across all tested configurations

validation_results.summary_finding: SwiLTra-Judge achieves highest correlation with human judgments (0.53) among all tested metrics, significantly outperforming XCOMET (0.48) and other automated metrics. Deduction-style prompting aligns better with human experts than absolute grading.

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM and human evaluate accuracy and completeness, but LLM uses broader criteria while human focuses specifically on legal accuracy and adherence to legal conventions.
